 UPDATE (Tuesday, Nov. 10) - The USSF-627 launch has been delayed again. Liftoff is now planned for Wednesday, Nov. 11, between 6:35 p.m. and 10:35 p.m. 
 According to Vandenberg base officials, a backup opportunity is available on Thursday if the launch is scrubbed on Wednesday.
___
 UPDATE (Monday, Nov. 9) - The launch has been pushed to Tuesday with the four-hour launch window opening shortly before 7 p.m.
___
 (Sunday, Nov. 8) - ORIGINAL STORY: SpaceX is planning to launch a Falcon 9 rocket out of Vandenberg Space Force Base. 
 The four-hour launch window is expected to open at 7:03 p.m. on Monday, November 9, carrying the USSF-627 mission.
 SpaceX says this will be the 7th flight for the first-stage booster supporting the mission.
 After stage separation, the first stage is expected to land on the 'Of Course I Still Love You' droneship in the Pacific Ocean.
 A live webcast will begin 10 minutes prior to the launch.
